621:
The 339 acre B.T. Brown Reservoir was constructed in 1984 for the purpose of drinking water supply and flood control. Coweta County will maintain the reservoir. The reservoir shall be governed by a management plan which addresses the recreational use of the reservoir and the maintenance of the buffer around the reservoir. The B.T. Brown Reservoir shall be specifically monitored for water quality standards by Coweta County. The reservoir shall be governed by a management plan which addresses the recreational use of the reservoir and the maintenance of the buffer around the reservoir.
(a) Recreational uses. The following recreational uses are either prohibited or restricted to protect the water quality of the reservoir for drinking purposes while optimizing its recreational benefits. Public recreation is not a primary purpose of the B.T. Brown Reservoir and such recreation is not encouraged.
(1) Swimming is prohibited.
(2) Fishing is allowed.
(3) Boating will be limited to electric, wind and manual boats only. No floating facilities of any type will be allowed on the reservoir pool.
(4) Boat docks or similar facilities are prohibited.
(5) Public access is not provided other than those existing legal rights-of-way.
(6) No private shoreline use permits will be issued.
(b) Buffer requirements. A buffer shall be maintained for a distance of 150 feet from the normal pool elevation of the reservoir. Should questions concerning the normal pool elevation arise, it shall be resolved by an engineering survey on a case-by-case basis. The 150-foot buffer shall not be encroached on by any impervious development.
(c) Reservoir monitoring. The B.T. Brown Reservoir is owned fee simple by Coweta County, Georgia. Coweta County will be responsible for the management of recreational uses and the buffer requirements. Coweta County shall be responsible for the monitoring of the water quality of the watershed. The county shall establish a monitoring plan as follows:
(1) General inspection of the B.T. Brown Watershed once every three years to monitor urban and rural development.
(2) Aerial inspection of the B.T. Brown Watershed once every five years to monitor urban and rural development.
(3) Establishment of three water quality monitoring points along the perennial streams feeding the reservoir in coordination with GA DNR EPD Water Quality Program.
(4) Sampling of water samples from the three monitoring points will be coordinated between the county and EPD for report scheduling and parameters with copies of said report filed with the EPD Water Resources Program.
(d) Enforcement. Violations of the criteria set forth in this plan for protecting the water quality of the B.T. Brown Reservoir shall be enforced by Coweta County, assigns or duly authorized agents. All incidents of littering, water pollution, or any other act which threatens water quality, after the first warning, shall be punishable by the maximum fine of $1,000.00 allowed by law in the Magistrate Court pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 15-10-60 et seq. This is in addition to any other punishment provided by other local, state or federal law.
(Ord. of 1-5-06)

(a) All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of the county for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state shall provide notice of such harvesting operations to the county public works director or his/her designee prior to entering onto the property if possible, but in no event later than 24 hours after entering onto the property. Further, such persons shall give notice of cessation of cutting within 24 hours after the job is completed. An appointment for ingress/egress inspection shall be scheduled 48 hours in advance of the inspection with the public works department to allow the public works director or his/her designee to inspect the site prior to any activity at the proposed ingress/egress location.
(b) The following minimum standards shall be met unless directed otherwise by the public works director or his/her designee and/or the code enforcement officer or his/her designee:
(1) Use geotextile underliner minimum 20 feet wide under gravel pad.
(2) Minimum drive width shall be 20 feet.
(3) Minimum thickness of six inches constructed of aggregate that is one and one-half inches to three and one-half inches in size with a minimum drive length of 50 feet.
(4) The county road, at each ingress/egress point, shall be posted with four 48-inch orange "Trucks Entering Highway" advance warning signs placed on the shoulder of the road at 500 feet and 1,000 feet intervals from both directions. Signs and posts shall confirm to the current edition of the Manual for Uniform Traffic Control Devices.
(c) The notice of harvesting operation required by this section shall be provided for each separate tract to be harvested. Such notice shall be made in such form as prescribed by rule or regulation from the director of the state forestry commission, and shall include the following information:
(1) A map of the area which identifies the location of the tract to be harvested and, as to those trucks which will be traveling to and from such tract for purposes of picking up and hauling loads of cut forest products, the main point of ingress to such tract from a public road and, if different, the main point of egress from such tract to a public road. If multiple points of ingress and/or ingress will be used, all such points shall be identified.
(2) A statement as to whether the timber will be removed pursuant to a lump sum sale, per unit sale, or owner harvest for purposes of ad valorem taxation under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7.5.
(3) The name, address, and daytime telephone number of the timber seller if the harvest is pursuant to a lump sum or per unit sale or of the timber owner if the harvest is an owner harvest.
(4) The name, business address, business telephone number, and nighttime or emergency telephone number of the person or firm harvesting such timber.
(d) Subject to the provisions of this section, the notice required may be submitted in person, transmitted electronically via telefacsimile or email, or by mail.
(e) Subject to the provisions of this section, upon notification published by the director of the state forestry commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons or firms wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required may do so at their option, and the county will accept notifications submitted in this manner.
(f) On or after a date specified and published by the director of the state forestry commission, use of the state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this section; on and after said date, submission of the notice by any means listed in section 30-229 (d) shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this section.
(g) The notice required by this section shall not be or remain effective unless and until the person or firm providing such notice has delivered to the county public works director or his/her designee a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in the state, protecting the county against any damage caused by such person or firm harvesting timber in the amount of $5,000.00; provided, however, that at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of $5,000.00 may be provided in lieu of a surety bond. Such bonds or letters of credit shall be subject to the conditions set forth in section 30-229 (h) and section 30-229 (i) of this section. No more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each person or firm harvesting timber, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
(h) The bond or letter of credit required by section 30-229 (g) of this section shall protect the county against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including treetops, debris, logs, pulpwood, and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damages or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within 500 feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation. The right of the county to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of section 30-229 (i) of this section shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
(i) When damage results from a person or firm's harvesting activities, the county public works director or his/her designee shall make and provide a written claim to the person or firm causing the damage within 30 business days after the public works department becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with section 30-229 (j) of this section, give the person or firm the opportunity to repair such damage within 30 days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the public works director or his/her designee determines the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the person or firm and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the responsible party and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided herein the public works director or his/her designee shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this section.
(j) Within 30 days of receipt of the written claim described in section 30-229 (i), the person or firm against whom the claim is submitted may:
(1) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the governing authority of the public works director or his/her designee. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the public works director or his/her designee, the public works director or his/her designee shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five business days to the responsible person or firm and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(2) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a 30-day extension to repair the damage from the public works director or his/her designee, provided that no extensions shall exceed 90 days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the public works director or his/her designee.
(3) Appeal the claim to the magistrate court of the county. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The magistrate court will hear evidence and arguments within 30 days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the 30-day period, or any extension thereof, required by section 30-229 (i) of this section. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the person or firm against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit, and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the county, the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment accordingly; the public works director or his/her designee shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court, up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(4) In the event the person or firm against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under section 30-229 (i) within the time required therein, such person or firm shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
(k) If the person or firm tendering a bond or letter of credit pursuant to the requirements of this section continues its timber harvesting operation beyond the calendar year in which the bond or letter of credit was issued, the person or firm continuing the timber harvesting operation shall tender a new bond or letter of credit within five business days after the first day of the new calendar year.
(l) In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this section is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered to the public works director or his/her designee within five business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to $7,500 after the first revocation, and $10,000 after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed $10,000.
(m) Submission of the notice required by this section shall authorize the person or firm submitting same to undertake the timber harvesting operation described in the notice and shall remain in effect until such time as the person or firm gives notice that the harvesting operation is complete; provided, however, that any change in the facts required to be provided for purposes of such notice, including but not limited to a change in the scope or extent of the operation, must be reported to the public works director or his/her designee within three business days after such change.
(n) Any person or firm that engages in a timber harvesting operation in the unincorporated portion of the county without complying with the notice requirements of this section shall be subject to a citation and trial, and upon conviction shall be fined in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00 for each violation.
(o) This section applies to activities which qualify as forestry land management practices or agricultural operations under O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17 (5) and (6) on land that is zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural or agricultural purposes. It shall not authorize land disturbing activities incidental to development in conflict with the limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17 (6).
(p) Consistent with O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24:
(1) No fee shall be charged to provide and submit the notice required by this section; and
(2) No permit, including a driveway permit, shall be required of the person or firm engaged in a timber harvesting operation as defined by said Code section. Persons and firms providing the notice required by this section may be asked to consult with county officials responsible for roads and public works for the purpose of minimizing damage to the county's roads, rights-of-way, and infrastructure, and are urged to follow recommendations from county officials. Notwithstanding the forgoing, the person or firm conducting the timber harvest operation bears ultimate responsibility for their actions, and nothing in this section shall preclude the governing authority of the county from taking any and all legal action necessary to protect its property and the health, safety, and welfare of its citizens.
(q) The provisions of this section are severable, and the invalidity of any phrase, clause, section, or part of this section shall not affect the validity or effectiveness of the remainder of this section.

704:
(a) Users of parks and recreation facilities shall be aware of weather conditions in the area and take proper precautions.
(b) The use of parks and recreation outdoor facilities or athletic fields is prohibited when, according to the National Weather Service, the following conditions exist:
(1) A tornado warning;
(2) A thunderstorm warning;
(3) Heat index or severe air quality warning;
(4) Any other severe weather warning or weather advisory; or
(5) Upon recommendation from Coweta County Emergency Management Agency.
(c) Parks and recreation facilities shall be closed to the public when the local school system is closed due to potential severe weather.
(d) Parks and recreation may postpone, reschedule, or cancel any event or activity if it is determined that a safety hazard exists.
(e) Priority for use of parks and recreation facilities and athletic fields will be given to parks and recreation programs and association programs for those associations under agreement with parks and recreation.
(f) It is prohibited to use a field currently undergoing maintenance or treatment or a field prepared for parks and recreation programs or association programs by associations under agreement with parks and recreation.
(g) Certain facilities and athletic fields are available for rent by contacting parks and recreation.
(h) Any event or activity promoted on any form of media, listing a parks and recreation facility as a place of assembly must be approved by the parks and recreation director.
(i) The use of parks and recreation facilities as a gathering place for commercial or non-sanctioned activities is strictly prohibited without approval from the parks and recreation director.
(j) The use of parks and recreation facilities should begin no earlier than 7:00 a.m. and end no later than 11:00 p.m., unless approved by the parks and recreation director and noted by signage.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21)
705:
The following is a list of prohibited items and activities on or about parks and recreation facilities athletic fields or any surrounding areas being property of the county:
(1) No alcoholic beverages.
(2) No littering.
(3) No explosive substances, including, but not limited to, fireworks.
(4) No glass containers.
(5) No smoking, use of tobacco products, or use of any smoking device that produces smoke, steam or vapor in accordance with chapter 2, article I, section 2-1 of the Coweta County Code of Ordinances.
(6) No profanity.
(7) No fighting or physical or verbal abuse.
(8) Pets are prohibited on athletic fields, playgrounds, and inside indoor facilities. Pets are allowed in designated areas. See section 46-33.
(9) Bicycles, scooters, skateboards, and other non-motorized recreational vehicles are only allowed in designated areas denoted by signage.
(10) No motorized recreational vehicles are allowed at parks and recreation facilities for any purpose unless approved by the parks and recreation director.
(11) No gambling or wagering allowed at parks and recreation facilities and/or on programs and activities taking place at parks and recreation facilities.
(12) No signage, including, but not limited to, banners, yard signs, or advertisements shall be placed at parks and recreation facilities, unless approved by the parks and recreation director.
(13) No admission fees, entry fees, or parking fees may be charged unless approved by the parks and recreation director. Parks and recreation may require documentation of collected fees and related operating costs.
(14) All vendors associated with any type of event, including, but not limited to, tournaments, training, clinics, or coaching events, must be approved by parks and recreation.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21)
706:
(a) Pets are prohibited from the below areas at parks and recreation facilities:
(1) Athletic fields;
(2) Near any athletic fields which are not enclosed by a barrier that restricts access;
(3) Bleachers, benches or similar designated viewing areas;
(4) Playgrounds; and
(5) Indoor facilities.
(b) All pets must be on a leash and under direct control of the pet owner at all times. The leash may not exceed six feet.
(c) No tethering.
(d) Pet access may be restricted for specific events or activities.
(e) All pet waste must be removed and disposed of in the proper location.
(f) Any pet showing aggressive behavior as determined by the parks and recreation director shall be removed immediately from the facility.
(g) Pet owners must follow and abide by all Coweta County ordinances, including chapter 10, Animals.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21)
707:
Coweta County Parks and Recreation recognizes a zero-tolerance policy at its parks and recreation facilities. Anyone found to be in violation will be subject to penalties, including, but not limited to, the following:
(1) Any person convicted by any court of a misdemeanor involving violence or convicted of any felony committed in connection with an event or activity, whether association sponsored, county sponsored, or related to general use at a parks and recreation facility shall be banned from parks and recreation facilities for a minimum period of two years or for the term of any sentence, including probation, imposed by any court deciding a particular case, whichever is greater.
(2) At the conclusion of the banned period as set out above, an individual banned from parks and recreation facilities may petition the parks and recreation director to have that individual's banned status lifted. The parks and recreation director, when considering a petition for lifting of banned status, shall consider the nature and severity of the crime committed and shall not be obligated to lift the banned status of any individual who, in the opinion of the parks and recreation director, poses a threat to the safety and health of citizens using parks and recreation facilities.
(3) Any person who petitions and his or her banned status is continued by the parks and recreation director may petition the county administrator for permission to use parks and recreation facilities and attend events and participate in activities at such facilities. If the county administrator continues the banned status of such person, the banned person may repeat the petition process annually thereafter.
(4) Nothing contained in this section shall imply that the parks and recreation director or the board of commissioners is ever obligated to lift a person's banned status from parks and recreation facilities, and, in appropriate cases, an individual may never be allowed to use parks and recreation facilities or attend events or participate in activities at such facilities.
(5) The parks and recreation director may ban a person charged with a misdemeanor involving violence or any felony from parks and recreation facilities pending the outcome of a court's determination of those charges.
(6) Any person that is banned from parks and recreation facilities for any period of time and is found at a parks and recreation facility during his/her banned period will be trespassing.
(7) All associations or groups using parks and recreation facilities shall establish bylaws governing the conduct of players, coaches, and spectators while attending or participating in activities at parks and recreation facilities. The bylaws must meet the standards defined in the association agreement and must be posted and available to all participants and volunteers.
(8) Any volunteer, coach, parent, participant, attendee, or other individual who is witnessed by parks and recreation staff, acting board members of an association under agreement with parks and recreation, or designated association volunteers, to be in violation of section 46-32, irrespective of whether the individual is removed from activity or facility upon observation of violation, will be banned from the related facility and activity for a period of time as to be determined by the parks and recreation director.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21; Ord. No. 006-25, 2-11-25)
708:
(a) In order for an association to operate programs at a parks and recreation facility, an association must enter into an association agreement with parks and recreation. Each association must meet all requirements and adhere to all rules and regulations defined in the association agreement.
(b) Each association must maintain 501c3 status and provide documentation verifying such status to parks and recreation.
(c) Each association must maintain a full governing board, and the election process must be transparent to all association participants.
(d) Each association must have established bylaws, and these must be adhered to by the association.
(e) Each association under agreement with parks and recreation shall pay a per participant user fee as established by the board of commissioners.
(f) The association shall not alter, add, remove, or improve parks and recreation facilities without written consent from the parks and recreation director. Any approved addition, alteration, or improvement will become and remain property of the county when completed.
(g) In the event of an association dissolving or not renewing the association agreement, any equipment or personal property left unclaimed at a parks and recreation facility will become property of parks and recreation after a 30-day period.
(h) The association agreement shall designate the athletic fields and related amenities such as concession stands, restrooms, and storage facilities which shall be utilized by the association. All other amenities are not to be restricted from public usage by the association during the operating hours of the parks and recreation facility.
(i) All Coweta County ordinances and rules apply to association events and activities and take precedence over the rules of an association.
(j) Parks and recreation reserves the right to enter into an association agreement at the sole discretion of the parks and recreation director. Parks and recreation reserves the right to terminate an association agreement due to failure of the association to comply with any Coweta County ordinance or parks and recreation policy or requirement. Parks and recreation reserves the right not to renew an association agreement at the sole discretion of the parks and recreation director. The decision by the parks and recreation director shall be in writing and may be appealed to the county administrator. The appeal shall be in writing and delivered to the county administrator within ten business days of receipt of the parks and recreation director's decision. The county administrator shall render a decision within 30 business days of receipt of the appeal. The county administrator's decision shall be final.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21)
709:
(a) Recreational league schedules and activities take precedence over tournaments and special events.
(b) Tournaments must be sponsored by parks and recreation or by an association under agreement with parks and recreation.
(c) In order to hold a tournament or special event at a parks and recreation facility, the sponsor must enter into an agreement with parks and recreation.
(d) Use of parks and recreation facilities for tournaments or special events will be subject to rental fees and other associated fees, as established by the board of commissioners.
(e) Prior to any advertising for a tournament or special event, all required forms and supporting documentation must be submitted and approved by parks and recreation and required fees must be paid.
(f) Tournaments must be sanctioned by a recognized athletic governing body.
(g) All vendors must be approved by parks and recreation and such vendors must maintain all necessary permits.
(h) No admission fees, entry fees, or parking fees may be charged unless approved by the parks and recreation director. Parks and recreation may require documentation of expected collections, related operating costs, and the intended use of excess collections, as well as final actual amounts.
(i) A sponsor must provide documentation verifying its 501c3 status to parks and recreation for any tournament or special event held with intent for charitable purposes.
(j) Tournament or special event sponsor will be required to leave parks and recreation facilities, including athletic fields, in the condition in which they were prior to the tournament.
(k) The tournament or special event sponsor must maintain a physical presence at the parks and recreation facility at all times during the tournament or special event.
(l) Parks and recreation reserves the right to set requirements based on the event type and scope. Requirements may include, but are not limited to, onsite security, traffic control, and/or emergency medical services.

The appeal shall be in writing and delivered to the county administrator within ten business days of receipt of the parks and recreation director's decision. The county administrator shall render a decision within 30 business days of receipt of the appeal. The county administrator's decision shall be final.

(o) All Coweta County ordinances and policies apply to tournaments and special events, including those related to weather and safety, and shall take precedence over the rules of the tournament or special event sponsor.

710:
Passive recreation is defined as the use of any parks and recreation facility for any use that is not related to an organized activity. Passive recreation includes, but is not limited to, use of greenspace, walking, jogging, biking, geocaching or any other use of passive elements at parks and recreation facilities.
(1) Prohibited activities include:
a. No camping;
b. No open fires;
c. No removal of artifacts or items of historical significance;
d. No hunting or fishing;
e. No harming or altering natural terrain, including, but not limited to, streams, creeks, and natural vegetation;
f. No intimidation or harming of wildlife; and
g. No motorized vehicles allowed on any trail system or pathway.
(2) All users must remain on designated trails or pathways. It shall be prohibited for anyone to cut or remove plants, trees, or other natural elements to create any sort of trail or pathway.
(3) All trails are designated for use, such as hiking or biking. It shall be prohibited for anyone to use trails in any manner beyond their designation.
(4) Any group or individual wishing to perform service work or projects at a parks and recreation facility must have the approval of the parks and recreation director.
(5) All passive elements at parks and recreation facilities will be open for public use from dawn to dusk, unless otherwise posted.
(6) State restrictions on usage of waterways apply where applicable.
(7) All Georgia Department of Natural Resources laws apply where applicable.
(8) All Coweta County ordinances and policies, including the entirety of chapter 46, Parks and Recreation, apply to passive recreation areas at parks and recreation facilities.
(Ord. No. 057-21, 12-14-21)

(a) Finding. There is hereby determined and declared a pressing, existing and future need for a development authority (as more fully described and defined in the Development Authorities Law, O.C.G.A. § 36-62-1 et seq.) to function in the county for the purpose of developing and promoting for the public good and general welfare, trade, commerce, industry and employment opportunities in said county, thereby promoting the general welfare of the citizenry and, in the furtherance of that purpose, to finance projects permitted thereby including projects for air and water pollution control facilities by industries.
(b) Activated. There is hereby activated in the county the public body corporate and politic known as the Development Authority of Coweta County, which was created upon the adoption and approval of the Development Authorities Law as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 36-62-1 et seq.

(d) Successors. If, at the end of any term of office of any director, a successor thereto shall not have been elected, then the director whose term of office shall have expired shall continue to hold office until his successor shall be so elected.
(e) Organization; operation. (f) Effect. The action taken in this section is not intended in any way to affect any public corporation, industrial development or payroll authority heretofore created by legislative act or constitutional amendment including, without limitation, its existence, purpose, organization, powers or function.

It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct, encroach upon, or injure materially any part of any county road or county rights-of-way. For purposes of this section, the term "obstruct" shall include, without limitation, the causing of any buildup of rock, gravel, mud, dirt, chemicals, or other materials by continued ingress and egress of vehicles or of any natural waters dammed or redirected by diversion to an extent which presents a hazard to the traveling public.

(a) No road, street, or thoroughfare shall be accepted by the board of commissioners as part of the public road system of the county, unless said road, street, or thoroughfare shall meet the following specifications:
(1) Public right-of-way as outlined in the development regulations or as determined by rezoning applications shall be dedicated to the county, but in no case shall the minimum width be less than 50 feet. 749:
Use of the Coweta County, Georgia public road system and rights-of-way for events such as, but not limited to, a foot race, vehicle race, bike race, bike ride, fun run or walk, filming, or car shows is unlawful unless such event has obtained a permit in accordance with this article.
As used in this article, the public road system is defined as the network of county owned and/or county-maintained roads and streets within the unincorporated area of Coweta County. As used in this definition, the phrase "county maintained" shall signify that county forces, equipment, and materials are utilized or have been utilized in the past to construct, preserve, or restore the road or street or a segment of the road or street to allow said road or street to serve a beneficial public purpose. The public road system shall not include private roads, private driveways, or driveways contained on ingress/egress easements that serve residential lots or tracts of land. The Coweta County Board of Commissioners shall have the authority to accept roads and streets into the public road system that have been constructed in accordance with the established county development regulations, standards, and specifications, as established in this chapter. The Coweta County Board of Commissioners shall also have the authority to remove any road or street from the public road system through the abandonment process established in O.C.G.A. § 32-7-2.
(Ord. No. 006-11, 4-5-11; Ord. No. 008-24, 6-4-24; Ord. No. 005-25, 2-11-25)
750:
A person seeking issuance of a right-of-way usage permit shall file an application with the parks and recreation department, event services division, on the application provided by the county.
(1) Filing period. An application for a right-of-way usage permit shall be filed not less than 90 days before the date of the event.
(2) Contents. The application for a right-of-way usage permit shall set forth the following information:
a. The name and contact information of the person or organization seeking the permit.
b. If the activity is proposed to be conducted for, on behalf of, or by an organization, the name and contact information of the headquarters of the organization, and of the authorized and responsible heads of that organization.
c. The name and contact information of the person who will be the activity leader and who will be responsible for its conduct.
d. The date when the activity is to be conducted.
e. The route to be traveled, the starting point and the termination point on a map in format as designated in application, to also include: proposed restroom locations, rest stops, water stations or temporary structures, where applicable.
f. The approximate number of persons who will participate in the event.
g. The hours the event will start and terminate.
h. A plan that identifies adequate provisions for parking and transportation of participants in the event where applicable.
i. If the event requires law enforcement protection or traffic control, the number of law enforcement officers to be employed by applicant to provide such protection and control.
j. Proof of adequate insurance to cover any damages or injuries arising from the event and a hold harmless agreement releasing Coweta County from any and all claims or damages arising from the permitting of the event.
k. Approval by the environmental health department of trash containment/removal and toilet facilities where applicable.
l. Approval by the sheriff of the route and determination that adequate precautions have been made to protect the participants and the traveling public.
m. When applicable, approval of the EMA director that adequate provisions have been made for emergency services and that the event will not interfere with movement of emergency response equipment in the case of an emergency. EMA director to be notified of all right-of-way usage permits issued.
n. Coweta County Fire Rescue to be notified of all right-of-way usage permits issued.
o. A plan for advance notification of the traveling public and the adjoining landowners of the event, as applicable.
p. Fees.
1. Application fee of $200.00 (non-refundable) to be paid at the time of application.
2. The board of commissioners may amend or revise these fees from time to time.
q. Any additional information which the county administrator, or his or her designee, shall find reasonably necessary to make a fair determination as to whether a right-of-way usage permit should be issued.
(Ord. No. 006-11, 4-5-11; Ord. No. 005-25, 2-11-25)
751:
The county administrator shall issue a right-of-way usage permit under this article when, from a consideration of the application and from any other information as may otherwise by obtained, the county administrator finds that:
(1) The conduct of the event will not substantially interrupt the safe and orderly movement of other traffic contiguous to the activity.
(2) The conduct of the event will not require the diversion of any of the county law enforcement officers to police the activity, but that adequate provision for police protection and traffic control have been made by the applicant and approved by the sheriff's department.
(3) The conduct of the event will not unreasonably interfere with the movement of emergency equipment en route to a fire or other emergency situation.
(4) The conduct of the event is not reasonably likely to cause injury to persons or property, to provoke disorderly conduct or create a disturbance.
(5) The event will not unreasonably burden the roads and rights-of-way of the county so as to substantially interfere with the normal use thereof by the public, but that adequate provisions for parking and transportation of participants in the activity have been made by the applicant.
(6) The conduct of the special event will not create a public nuisance or interfere with the quiet enjoyment of the neighboring property owners.
(Ord. No. 006-11, 4-5-11)
752:
A right-of-way usage permit issued pursuant to this article may be suspended or revoked by the sheriff, public safety director (or EMA director), or county administrator for due cause for violation of this chapter; for failure to comply with the terms of the permit or when such violation results in an emergency situation in which continued operation of the activity of permittee endangers the health, safety, or welfare of the public.
(Ord. No. 006-11, 4-5-11)
753:
Failure to obtain a right-of-way usage permit will result in violation of this chapter and shall be guilty of an offense against the county, punishable upon citation before the magistrate court. Any person convicted of violating any provision of this chapter shall be punished in accordance with section 1-15.

760:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned sign. Any sign that contains or exhibits broken panels, visible rust, visible rot, damaged support structures, or missing letters or which is otherwise dilapidated, unsightly, or unkempt, and for which no person accepts maintenance responsibility.
Animated sign. Any sign, or part of a sign, that uses any movement or change of lighting or color to depict action or create a special effect or scene.
Audible sign. Any sign which emits a sound which is audible or emits a signal which can be converted into audible sounds, whether by radio or other means.
Awning/canopy sign. Any sign that is a part of, or attached to, an awning, canopy or other fabric, plastic or structural protective cover over a door, entrance, window, or outdoor service area. A marquee is not a canopy.
Banner. A sign other than a flag with or without characters, letters, illustrations or ornamentation applied to cloth, paper, or fabric that is intended to be hung without a frame. Neither flags nor canopy signs are considered banners.
Beacon. Any light with one or more beams directed into the atmosphere or directed at one or more points not on the same lot as the light source; also, any light with one or more beams that rotate or move.
Canopy sign. A sign imposed upon or painted on any roof-like structure either permanently or temporarily, extended over an entry sidewalk or walkway, which may be mounted flush or suspended.
Changeable copy sign. Any sign that incorporates changing lights, lettering, or images to form a sign message or messages, whether such changes are accomplished electronically or manually.
Department means the community development department, including the development review division; the development inspections division; the zoning, building and licensing division; the county planner; and the code enforcement division.
Director means the director of the community development department or their designee responsible for administering and ensuring compliance with all provisions of this article.
Fall zone. An area equal to 133 percent of the height of the structure in every direction.
Flag. Any fabric or bunting containing colors, patterns, or symbol used as a symbol of a government or other entity or organization.
Free-standing sign. A sign that is not mounted on a principal building.
Lot. A parcel of land that is of sufficient size to meet minimum zoning requirements for lot area, coverage, and use and that can provide such yards and other open spaces as required by the zoning standards.
Monument sign. A permanent ground sign designed so that the base of the sign face is flush with the supporting base, and the supporting base is flush with the ground and extends the full width of the sign face or a sign that is attached to a monument face.
Moving sign. A sign which revolves, rotates, swings, undulates, or otherwise attracts attention through the structural movement of parts.
Nonconforming sign. Any sign that does not conform to the provisions of this chapter at the effective date of this chapter, or any amendment thereto.
Obscene. Material is obscene if to the average person, applying contemporary community standards, taken as a whole, it predominantly appeals to the prurient interest, that is, a shameful or morbid interest in nudity, sex or excretion; the material taken as a whole lacks serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value; and the material depicts or describes, in a patently offensive way, sexual conduct specifically defined as:
(a) Acts of sexual intercourse, heterosexual or homosexual, normal or perverted, actual or simulated;
(b) Acts of masturbation;
(c) Acts involving excretory functions or lewd exhibition of the genitals;
(d) Acts of bestiality or the fondling of sex organs of animals; or
(e) Sexual acts of flagellation, torture, or other violence indicating a sadomasochistic sexual relationship.
Out-of-store marketing device. Any facility or equipment which is located outside of a primary building on a site zoned for nonresidential uses, which is used for the primary purpose of providing a product or service without the owner's or agent's immediate presence, and which is manufactured to include a color, form, graphic, illumination, symbol, and/or writing thereon to communicate information regarding the product or service provided thereby to the public. Examples of out-of-store marketing devices include: fuel pumps, bank ATM units, vending machines, newspaper racks, drink machines, ice boxes, and phone books. Where such out-of-store marketing devices are too small to be legible to the traveling public on neighboring rights-of-way and are otherwise nonremovable without damage to the equipment's surface, they do not require a permit and are not subject to overall sign limitations for the lot on which they appear.
Pennant, streamer. Any lightweight plastic, fabric, or other material, whether or not containing a message of any kind, suspended from a rope, wire, or string, usually in a series, designed to move in the wind.
Permit means a sign permit reviewed, approved, and issued by the department.
Permittee. The person and/or entity owning or leasing the land on which the sign is erected or for which an application has been submitted.
Portable sign. A sign which is not permanently affixed to the ground or to a structure, including but not limited to signs on trailers or signs mounted or painted on vehicles which are parked in such a manner as to serve the purpose of a sign.
Principal building. The building in which the principal use of the lot is conducted. Nonresidential lots with multiple principal uses may have multiple principal buildings, but storage buildings, garages, and other structures with clearly accessory uses shall not be considered principal buildings.
Projecting sign. A sign attached to and projecting from the wall or overhang of a building that has a plane that is at a 90-degree angle from the wall.
Public sign. Any sign erected by a governmental entity.
Roof sign. Any sign erected and constructed wholly on and over the roof of a building, or supported by the roof structure.
Sign. A sign is an object, device, display, or structure, or thereof, displayed outdoors or visible from a public way, which is used to advertise, identify, display, direct or attract attention to an object, person, institution, organization, business, product, service, event or location; or to express a point of view, by any means including words, letters, figures, designs, symbols, advertising flags, fixtures, colors, illuminations or projected images.
Sign, traffic control. A sign to regulate the safe and ordered flow of vehicular and pedestrian traffic.
Suspended sign. A sign attached to the underside of a horizontal plane or arm and is supported by the horizontal plane. The horizontal plane or arm is attached to a column or wall.
Temporary sign. Any sign that is not permanently mounted and is mounted on a stake or metal frame with a thickness or diameter not greater than one and one-half inches.
Wall sign. A sign which is mounted parallel on the exterior surface of a building.
Window sign. Any sign that is placed inside a window or upon the window panes or glass, either inside or outside the building, and is visible from the exterior of the structure.

761:
(a) Permit required. A permit shall be required for the erection, alteration or reconstruction of any sign unless otherwise noted and shall be issued by the department after approval by the director in accordance with the regulations contained in this chapter. This requirement includes, but is not limited to, conversion of a sign to tri-vision, LED, or similar technology, among other work.
(b) Design and materials.
(1) All signs shall be designed and constructed in accordance with applicable provisions of the rules and regulations of the department.
(2) Unless provided otherwise, all freestanding signs in nonresidential zoning districts shall be monument signs.
(3) a. The base and structure of monument permitted signs located in the quality development corridor (QDC) overlay zoning district shall be composed of brick, stone, masonry-backed stucco, wood or other category A materials as detailed in subsection 246.1.5(1)(a) of the zoning and development ordinance. A combination of two of more materials is allowed.
b. The base and structure for permitted signs located outside the quality development corridor (QDC) overlay zoning district shall be composed of brick, stone, masonry-backed stucco, wood or other category A materials as detailed as acceptable in subsection 246.1.5(1)(a) of the zoning and development ordinance. A combination of two or more materials is allowed. In addition, aluminum sheeting shall be a permitted material meeting the following specifications;
(i) The thickness of aluminum shall be a minimum of 0.040 gauge thickness.
(ii) The base shall be a minimum of a four-sided construction (front, rear, right and left sides). A top shall be required only if needed to screen any mechanical or structural components on the interior of the sign.
(iii) The base shall be neither weight bearing nor support structure, but only serving as a mechanism to conceal the erection poles, thus completing the monolithic monument requirement.
(iv) The base shall be finished to give the appearance of masonry, textured finish or may be painted in a similar fashion.
(c) Maintenance.
(1) The area on private property around the sign on which it is erected shall be properly maintained clear of brush, trees, and other obstacles so as to make signs readily visible;
(2) All burned out bulbs or damaged panels must be replaced;
(3) All sign copy shall be maintained securely to the face and all missing copy must be replaced;
(4) All signs shall be maintained in good structural condition at all times so that the public and traffic safety are not compromised; and
(5) All signs shall present a neat and orderly appearance, without rust or holes on or in the sign or sign structure, or broken, missing, loose or bent parts, faded, or flaking paint, nonoperative or particularly nonoperative illuminating or mechanical devices or missing letters in sign copy.
(6) It shall be the responsibility of the sign owner to maintain and ensure compliance with the provisions of this chapter.
(d) Measurement of maximum height of signs. The height of all signs shall be measured from the grade at the right-of-way boundary line or the grade of the sign site if such grade is higher than the grade at the boundary line of the street right-of-way to the uppermost part of the sign face, base or structure. If the sign is located below the grade at the boundary line of the street right-of-way, sign height shall be measured from the edge of the right-of-way to the uppermost part of the sign face, base or structure.
(e) Computation of sign area.
(1) The area of the sign shall be computed from the algebraic sum of the actual sign configuration, be it square, rectangle, circle, oval or other polygon shape. The area shall be measured from the outer dimensions of the frame, trim or molding by which the sign is enclosed, where they exist, or from the outer edge of the signboard where they do not exist.
(2) When a sign consists of individual letters, symbols or characters, its area shall be computed as the area of the smallest rectangle which encloses all the letters, symbols and characters.
(f) Minimum sign setbacks. Except as otherwise specifically provided, for any freestanding signs, the minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater, and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing.
(g) Illumination.
(1) Nonresidential districts. No sign shall be illuminated by lights that flash, move, change in intensity, or turn on intermittently more than once per day, except as provided herein. To prevent glare visible from a public street or adjoining property, the beam of any light shall be directed so as not to be visible beyond the sign at which it is directed, and the light source shall not be visible from any point on an adjacent property or the public right-of-way. Light from any illuminated sign shall not be of an intensity or brightness which will interfere with the peace, comfort, convenience, and general welfare of residents or occupants of adjacent properties or vehicular traffic on adjacent roadways.
(2) Residential districts. Signs located in residential districts shall not be illuminated other than signs at the entrance of the subdivision.
(h) Reserved.
(i) Sign message. In any zoning district, any sign, display, or devise allowed under this chapter may contain any lawful noncommercial or commercial message except as expressly provided herein. No provision of this chapter shall be construed to allow regulation of signs based on the content of the sign message.

762:
The following signs are allowed with a permit.
(a) Wall signs. Wall signs shall be permitted on the wall facing a public street unless that building has public street frontage on more than one side, in which case, additional wall signs are allowed on the side facing the street, subject to the following:
(1) Wall signs are allowed in all nonresidential zoning districts and in residential zoning districts that are subject to a conditional use permit or that are at least ten acres and have a permitted nonresidential use.
(2) If a structure is located on a lot that has no street frontage, wall signs shall be permitted on any single facade.
(3) Wall signs attached flat against the exterior surface of a building may extend not more than 24 inches from the wall.
(4) For buildings 50,000 square feet or less in size, the total area for wall signage shall not exceed 25 percent of the total area of the one building facade upon which the signage is placed or 200 square feet, whichever is less. For buildings over 50,000 square feet in size, the total area for wall signage shall not exceed ten percent of the total area of the one building facade upon which the signage is placed or 400 square feet, whichever is less. A sign directory is a wall sign. For buildings with multiple tenants having store fronts only, the facade rented by the tenant shall be considered as wall area for a sign; and tenant spaces of 50,000 square feet or less in size shall be calculated at 25 percent of the total area of the one tenant space on which the signage is placed or 200 square feet, whichever is less.
(5) Reserved.
(6) Wall signs shall not extend above the eave line or top of a parapet on the wall to which it is attached.
(b) Canopy signs. In nonresidential districts only, one canopy sign may cover 25 percent of a canopy but shall not exceed a length of 20 feet and a maximum area of 40 square feet and shall be at least 8 feet above the lowest ground elevation.
(c) Banners. Banners shall be permitted only by the issuance of a permit under the following conditions:
(1) Banners are allowed in nonresidential zoning districts, residential zoning districts that are subject to a conditional use permit, and residentially zoned parcels that combine to create a single nonresidential use on at least ten acres.
(2) One banner may be erected for no more than 30 days.
(3) The maximum size of the banner shall not exceed 35 square feet and the height shall not exceed five feet.
(4) Only one banner will be permitted for particular lot during a 90-day period.
(5) The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a banner be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
(d) Projecting signs. One projecting nonilluminated sign per door entrance used shall be allowed, provided the following:
(1) Projecting signs are allowed in all nonresidential zoning districts.
(2) The sign is no more than three square feet in area;
(3) Is uniform in size, material, color and shape and is placed in an equivalent location to other such signs located on the same building;
(4) Is suspended from the eave or sofit of the building or extends from the wall; and
(5) Maintains a minimum of eight feet clearance between the bottom of the sign and the walkway below;
(6) Shall not extend vertically beyond the window sill of the second story.
(e) Menu boards. Restaurant menu boards are allowed subject to the following regulations:
(1) Menu boards are allowed in all nonresidential zoning districts.
(2) No more than 35 square feet in area.
(3) No more than five feet in height.
(4) No part of the sign shall be legible by the traveling public.
(f) Residential subdivision entrance. No more than two freestanding monument signs or two suspended signs attached to a wall or column shall be allowed to be placed on residentially zoned property subject to the following:
1. The sign face for a monument sign shall not exceed 40 square feet in area and ten feet in height. The sign face for the suspended sign shall not exceed 16 square feet in area and ten feet in height. Such signs shall be secured to a support structure to prevent the sign(s) from becoming airborne.
2. If the sign structure is attached to a decorative wall or fence, the decorative wall or fence shall not exceed eight feet in height. The post and/or columns of the decorative wall or fence shall not exceed ten feet in height.
3. Such signs shall not be internally illuminated.
4. The permit shall not be issued until after the final plat is recorded.
5. The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
(g) Signage during construction. Four additional signs shall be allowed during construction of a residential or nonresidential subdivision. The sign shall not be internally illuminated.
(1) Duration. The sign shall be allowed beginning with the issuance of a land disturbance permit and ending with the issuance of a certificate of occupancy or installation of a permanent sign at the subdivision entrance, whichever comes first.
(2) Size. The sign shall not exceed 16 square feet in area and 86 feet in height.
(3) Location The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
(h) Monument signs. The owner of property or the owner's agent may apply for a permit for monument signs subject to the following:
(1) Signs permitted by this section are allowed only in nonresidential zoning districts, residential zoning districts that are subject to a conditional use permit, and residentially zoned parcels that combine to create a single nonresidential use on at least ten acres.
(2) The maximum sign area of the sign shall be 100 square feet for multiple user lots and 60 square feet for single user lots. Maximum sign areas shall apply to each face separately, but no freestanding sign shall have more than two faces. Where two sign faces are located in a "V" formation, the angle between the two sign faces shall not be greater than 60 degrees.
(3) The maximum height of the sign is eight feet.
(4) The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
(5) One monument sign is permitted for each street on which the parcel has at least 50 feet of road frontage.
(6) Lots that contain an interstate sign shall not be allowed to place a monument sign on the lot.
(7) Monument sign design.
Type A: A permanent ground sign designed so the base of the sign face is flush with the supporting base, and the supporting base is flush with the ground and extends the full width of the sign face provided the sign face does not project more than 12 inches from the monument face and the sign base does not extend greater than 24 inches from all sides of the sign face or structure.
Type B: A sign that is attached to a monument face provided the sign face does not project more than 12 inches from the monument face and the sign base does not extend greater than 24 inches from all sides of the sign face or structure.
(i) Interstate sign. One interstate sign per quadrant location, as defined below, of any interchange adjacent to the interstate highway is permitted under the following conditions:
(1) The sign must be located within 600 feet of the right-of-way of Interstate 85.
(2) The signs must be located within 600 feet of an ongoing commercial or industrial activity.
(3) The parcel upon which the sign is located must be zoned for nonresidential use.
(4) The signs are restricted to the quadrant area of 1,200 feet long beginning 500 feet from the point where the pavement widens on the main travel way to accommodate the longest entrance or exit ramp.
(5) The sign may be a maximum size of 600 square feet inclusive of any border and trim, but excluding the base apron, supports, and other structural members. A uniform size requirement of 12 feet in height by 50 feet of length shall be strictly adhered to.
(6) The maximum sign height is 50 feet.
(7) The sign must be located on a parcel of at least one acre.
(8) The sign must be located on a parcel that allows for a clear fall zone such that no building or other structure shall be located within the fall zone.
(9) The signs allowed by this section may be pole signs.
(10) Lots that contain a monument sign shall not be allowed to place an interstate sign on the lot.
(11) The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
(j) Industrial park entrance. No more than two signs attached to a base, wall, or column shall be allowed to be placed on industrial zoned property (LM or M) subject to the following:
(1) The total area of the sign face(s) shall not exceed 750 square feet in area and eight feet in height. If the sign face is separated from the base, wall, or column, the height of the support structure shall not exceed 12 inches and shall be included in the maximum height allowed.
(2) If applicable, decorative wall or fence shall not exceed eight feet in height. The post and/or columns of the decorative wall or fence shall not exceed ten feet in height.
(3) The sign may be lighted internally.
(4) The permit shall not be issued until after the final plat is recorded.
(5) The minimum front setback shall be 15 feet from the edge of the pavement or outside of the right-of-way, whichever is greater and ten feet from the side and rear lot lines. However, in no case will a sign be allowed to obscure vision at a street or driveway intersection, or railway crossing. For traffic safety, signs shall not be located within the triangular area on a corner lot formed by measuring 20 feet along both street side property lines from their intersection.
