Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, ch. 14; planning, ch. 50; utilities, ch. 78; zoning, app. A.
825:
No person shall operate or permit a taxicab or any other automobile owned or controlled by him to be operated as a vehicle for hire in Coweta County without having first obtained a certificate from the county authorizing such operation.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
826:
Where the business is located in the county, no taxicab or any other automobile for hire shall operate in the county unless the owner thereof shall maintain a place of business from a building located on property within a commercially zoned district in which vehicles for hire is a permitted use in accordance with the most recently adopted zoning map and have first obtained certification of compliance from the community development department.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
827:
No person shall operate a taxicab or any other vehicle for hire unless such person possesses the proper driver's license as required under the laws of the state and is not less than 18 years of age and has obtained a permit as set forth herein.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
831:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Applicant means an individual registering a business authorized herein.
Application means a form supplied by the county for the purpose of registering a business authorized herein.
Business means the business of operating or owning a taxicab business.
Certificate means certificate issued or approved by the director authorizing the holder thereof to conduct a taxicab business within the county.
County means Coweta County, Georgia.
Closely held corporation means a corporation not traded or listed on any stock exchange and which has fewer than 25 shareholders.
Convicted or conviction shall include a plea of nolo contendere.
Department means the community development department, including the development review division; the development inspections division; the zoning, building and licensing division; the county planner; and the code enforcement division.
Director means the director of the community development department or their designee responsible for administering and ensuring compliance with all provisions of this article.
Driver, operator means any person in charge of or driving or operating a taxicab, as defined herein, whether as owner, agent, employee or otherwise.
Driver's permit means the permission granted by the governing body to a person to drive a taxicab within the county.
Employee means an individual whose work is performed under the direction and supervision of the employer and whose employer withholds FICA, federal income tax, or state income tax from such individual's compensation or whose employer issues to such individual for purposes of documenting compensation a form IRS W-2 but not a form IRS 1099.
Highway means any of the public streets, alleys, lanes, boulevards, avenues, drives, circles, or roads of the county.
Individual means a natural person.
Interest in a business means an interest held by an owner or co-owner of a registered business; by a partner of a general or limited partnership which owns or co-owns a registered business; a stockholder of five percent or more shares in any closely held corporation which owns or co-owns a registered business; or anyone sharing in the income or corpus of any trust or estate having such an interest; or a person having subscriptions, options, and/or warranty for purchase of five percent or more of a closely held corporation's stock or 50 percent or more of any corporation's stock.
Memorandum certificate means the card issued to a taxicab owner to display within the taxicab indicating that such taxicab has been issued a certificate.
Non-emergency transport vehicles means a vehicle used to transport an individual for a non-urgent procedure or elective care where there is no need for immediate assistance.
Owner means a person having an interest in a business, including a stockholder and to whom a certificate for operating a taxicab has been or is to be issued.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business, trust, receiver, fiduciary or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public, or any entity.
Taxicab means any motor vehicle seating eight or fewer persons and the driver, operating upon any street on call or demand, accepting or soliciting passengers indiscriminately for hire between such points along such streets as may be directed by the passengers being so transported. This definition shall include non-emergency transport vehicles.
Vehicles for hire means taxicab as defined herein or limousine as defined in section 68-111.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
832:
All taxicabs operating within the county shall comply with all laws of the United States of America, the state and the county regulating the speed, the operation of motor vehicles and the requirements for safety equipment and devices. All passengers, whether adult, children or infants shall use the required passenger restraint devices including child restraints as necessary. Drivers shall show due regard for the safety, comfort and convenience of passengers, for the safe and careful transportation of property and for the safety of the general public.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
833:
(a) Information required. All motor vehicles operated as taxicabs in the county shall be marked on the outside with the following information with respect thereto:
(1) The name of the owner of the taxicab.
(2) The word "taxicab" or "taxi."
(3) If a fleet of more than one taxicab is operated by one company or owner, a number shall be assigned to each vehicle, prominently displayed and identifying.
(4) Any other information which may be deemed necessary to identify such vehicle as required by the director.
(b) Affixing information. The above markings or identification shall be prominently displayed on both sides of the vehicles operated as taxicabs in letters of not less than three inches in height and must be printed so that the identification may be easily read at a distance of at least 50 feet. Such information may be displayed on vehicle with paint, by stencil, by decals or with magnetic signs.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
834:
No person shall be permitted to ride on the fender, hood, roof or any other exterior portion of a taxicab.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
837:
All persons applying for a certificate provided for in section 68-1 shall do so in writing to the director on the form provided by county. Such applicant shall furnish all information required by such form in complete detail and shall certify under oath to the correctness of the information.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
838:
The director shall investigate the application provided for in section 68-41 and shall grant the certification if the application meets all requirements of this chapter and payment of the required fee. The director shall also issue a memorandum certificate for each taxicab authorized by the county.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
839:
All certificates shall expire on December 31 of each year, including the year of issue, but may be reinstated by the director for the following year, provided that there has been no revocation thereof and further provided that all license fees required to be paid have been paid.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
840:
(a) Duty of operator. Prior to placing a taxicab in service, and prior to annually renewing the permit, any operator shall register that vehicle with the director, providing a complete and true description of such vehicle to include the serial number, make, model and color; and a statement from an automotive service excellency (ASE) certified mechanic concerning the safety of the vehicle.
(b) Duty of director. The director shall maintain a file on each operator, including the description of each vehicle registered as required by this section, and he may issue identification numbers for each registered vehicle. The director may make inspections at any time to assure that the taxicabs in operation are registered and in full compliance with this article.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
841:
Should the director issue identification numbers, these numbers shall be affixed by decal or similar means in the rear window of the vehicle on the driver's side.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
842:
Every person operating a taxicab in the county or the owner of any such taxicab shall provide the director with a copy of the insurance certificate showing that such vehicle is properly insured in accordance with the laws of the state, and such insurance company shall be properly licensed to do business in the state and the county.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
843:
The county shall be given a minimum of ten days' written notice of cancellation of vehicular insurance covering the operation of taxicabs.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
844:
The director may suspend from operation any taxicab found to be unsafe, and any vehicle so suspended shall not be permitted to again operate until repaired and put in proper condition for use. Prior to returning to service, such taxicab shall be inspected by an ASE certified mechanic and a statement from the mechanic shall be submitted to the director.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
845:
(a) Notice required. If any owner or operator of a taxicab in the county shall sell, trade or exchange any taxicab being operated in the county and substitute another car therefore, it shall be the duty of the seller to notify the director within 24 hours of the sale, trade or exchange of the vehicle, and such owner or operator shall provide the director with the identification number of such vehicle under which the vehicle is identified on the insurance policy on file.
(b) Transfer of insurance required. It shall be the duty of such owner or operator of the car substituted to furnish the director written endorsement of the insurance company issuing the vehicular insurance policy showing that the additional vehicle is properly insured under the terms of the policy.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19; Ord. No. 036-19, 9-5-19)
846:
Each taxicab operator licensed in the county shall post, at a conspicuous place in his taxicabs, a schedule of rates, such schedule clearly showing distances and prices thereof. Each such operator shall furnish a similar copy of such rates so posted in his taxicabs to the director.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19; Ord. No. 036-19, 9-5-19)
847:
It shall be unlawful for any taxicab owner or operator to fail to post or publish the rates as required in section 68-50 and, by himself or through his drivers, to charge rates in excess of those published. If the rates are not posted and/or there is an excessive charge, the board of commissioners may call for a hearing in which the owner or operator is allowed to appear and be heard and present evidence on the matter. If it is determined that this section or section 68-50 has been violated, the board may revoke or suspend such owner's or operator's license.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
848:
Every owner of a taxicab or taxicab company shall comply with the following regulations:
(1) Condition of taxicab. All taxicabs shall be maintained in a clean and safe condition at all times.
(2) Record of calls. The owner or taxicab company shall keep a record of all telephone calls for taxicabs service for a minimum of 30 days for use, if needed, by the police department.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
849:
Taxicab companies shall not be permitted to have their offices below street level.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
852:
Before any person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county, he shall first pay to the director a registration fee as set by the board of commissioners and shall make a written and signed application to such director which shall contain the following information: name, residence, telephone number, age, date of birth, height, weight, hair color, color of eyes, number of years experience driving motor vehicles, whether he has been convicted of any felonies, misdemeanors or traffic ordinance violations, and if so, giving the dates and details and any other information requested by the director. The applicant shall also provide the names, addresses and telephone numbers of at least two references who can answer questions related to the background investigation which will be conducted by the director. If the applicant desires a permit to drive for the owner of a taxicab business, the applicant shall include the name of such owner. Such permit shall be issued and renewed on an annual basis.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
853:
(a) Issuance of permit; contents. After receipt of the application for permit provided for in section 68-71, the director shall consider the same, and if satisfied from such application and other evidence that the applicant is a fit and proper person to safely drive a taxicab in the county, and that the application complies with the provisions of this article and the traffic ordinances of the county, the permit shall be granted to the applicant and signed by the director. The permit shall contain the name and description of the applicant and such other data as the director deems proper.
(b) Denial of permit. The Sheriff shall investigate each applicant for a taxicab license. He shall also check the record of each applicant for felony convictions and/or traffic violations. Any person who has been convicted of, pled guilty to or forfeited bonds as being in violation of traffic offenses totaling more than 20 points, as provided by state law within the five years immediately prior to his application for a license, shall not be entitled to a permit to operate a taxicab or vehicle for hire within the county.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
854:
The name and picture of each taxicab driver, shall be attached to the permit issued to such driver, and such permit, picture and signature shall be prominently displayed inside each taxicab such driver operates.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
855:
Each permit granted for the privilege of driving a taxicab upon the roads of the county is subject to suspension or revocation, or both, by the director whenever the holder of such permit violates or fails to comply with a provision of this article, whether or not there has been a trial of such driver before any court. The director shall notify such driver in writing of the suspension or revocation.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
856:
Any person to whom the director has denied a permit to drive a taxicab, and any person whose permit has been suspended or revoked shall have the right to appeal to the board of commissioners, which may, by resolution, grant or deny relief as may appear proper to the board of commissioners and in accordance with the terms and intent of this article.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
857:
Because of the necessity of providing for the public safety and the public health, and because the driving of taxicabs upon the roads of the county is a mere privilege and not a right, a wide discretion shall be vested in the director in granting or refusing permits, suspending and revoking such permits and carrying out the provisions and intent of this article.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 014-19, adopted March 26, 2019, changed the title of § 68-76 from "Same—Extent of authority of business license director" to read as herein set out.
858:
The board of commissioners shall not be limited in the control over permits to operate taxicabs to cases appealed from the action of the director, nor to cases arising because of violations of the terms of this article. The board of commissioners shall have the power to suspend or revoke any permit granted for the driving of a taxicab on county roads whenever it finds that such suspension or revocation would be in the public interest.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
859:
(a) All persons applying for permits to drive or already driving taxicabs on county roads shall be in good health and be capable of physically performing the work as a driver.
(b) No person shall drive a taxicab when on account of poor eyesight not corrected by glasses, or on account of bodily or mental infirmity, or being afflicted by infectious or contagious disease or for other reasons, he is unable safely to drive a taxicab upon such roads.
(c) Should the director have concerns about the capability of any applicant to comply with the section, the director may require that such applicant, at his own expense, undergo a physical examination by a licensed physician. Refusal of the applicant to undergo the examination shall constitute grounds for denial of the permit.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
860:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county until he has had his fingerprints taken by the sheriff department.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
861:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county who has been convicted or pled guilty to an offense constituting a felony; however, if such person has had his civil and political rights restored and/or been given a pardon, such felony conviction will not bar such person from receiving a permit authorizing him to drive a taxicab in the county.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
862:
All taxicab drivers shall be neat in appearance while on duty, clean in person and dress. No person shall operate a taxicab without shoes and each driver must wear shirt, blouse or top.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
863:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county until he has shown, upon examination by the director, a familiarity with the provisions of this article, the same to be furnished by the director to each driver.
(Ord. of 10-4-05; Ord. No. 014-19, 3-26-19)
864:
A person driving a taxicab upon the roads of the county shall bring the vehicle to a full stop immediately upon command of a member of the sheriff department and any other law enforcement officer, and shall proceed only as lawfully directed by such officer.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
865:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county while under the influence of alcoholic beverages or narcotics or who habitually uses alcoholic beverages or narcotics.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
866:
(a) Prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person operating a licensed taxicab service in the county or any driver operating a taxicab in the county under such license, knowingly to haul any form of open alcoholic beverages, narcotics, or other illegal substances in such taxicab.
(b) Revocation of operator's license. If the driver of any taxicab in the county knowingly allows or permits alcoholic beverages or narcotics to be hauled or consumed in the taxicab operated by him, the holder or owner of the license issued by the county, under which such taxicab is being operated, shall forfeit his license and the license shall be automatically revoked. If any license is forfeited and revoked because a driver is guilty of hauling alcoholic beverages or narcotics, the licensee shall have the right of a hearing before the board of commissioners at such time and place as the board may designate. Pending such hearing before the board of commissioners, the owner or holder of such license shall not operate the taxicab service under and by virtue of any such license.
(c) Forfeiture of driver's rights. It shall be unlawful for any driver guilty of knowingly hauling alcoholic beverages or narcotics in any taxicab driven by him to again drive a taxicab in the county.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
867:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county transporting prostitutes or soliciting or transporting persons for the purposes of illegal actions.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
868:
No driver of a taxicab shall cruise in search of passengers at any time but shall proceed from an origin by the most convenient and direct route to the required destination. When a taxicab is empty of passengers it shall, if awaiting a radio call for another trip, remain parked at a convenient location in the general area of the last destination, or proceed directly to its headquarters or to a designated cabstand without soliciting passengers in route.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
869:
No person shall drive a taxicab upon the roads of the county when such vehicle contains passengers in excess of the maximum number for which the vehicle was designed.
(Ord. of 10-4-05)
